podcast.title: Gramophone Debut (1887)
podcast.body: Emil Berliner's gramophone, which debuted ten years after Edison's talking machine, was another pioneering device for capturing sound. Like Edison's invention, it was limited to about three minutes of recording, a constraint that helped establish the standard length for popular songs. "Emil Berliner's gramophone, which debuted ten years later, were the first machines able to capture sound up to three minutes at a time."

podcast.title: Early Flat Disc Commercial Failure
podcast.body: Despite Bernliner's innovations, his early flat discs, composed of shellac and mineral, suffered a significant commercial failure. They were prohibitively expensive, extremely heavy, and highly susceptible to breaking when dropped, eventually being superseded by plastic vinyl discs as advancements in plastic material knowledge and casting techniques emerged in the early 20th century. "acabó siendo un enorme fracasso, eran carísimos, eran pesadísimos, se rompían al caral suelo."

podcast.title: Shellac Disc Invention (Late 19th Century)
podcast.body: Bernliner revived Thomas Edison's original idea of a flat disc, inventing the first "vinyl" disc made from shellac and mineral, often pizarra (slate), meaning early records were literally stone. These discs were remarkably resistant to the erosion from rudimentary steel needles and recording methods, but the nascent understanding of plastic materials made them costly and heavy precursors to modern vinyl. "Bernliner inventó el disco de goma lacacom mineral, que casi siempre solía ser pizarra."

podcast.title: Sound Recording Innovations (Late 19th Century)
podcast.body: Towards the end of the 19th century, around 1895, Bernliner significantly advanced sound recording technology by discovering a superior method for engraving sound into grooves. He is recognized as the inventor of sound formats, the process of sound recording, and the first gramophones, effectively laying the groundwork for subsequent physical music formats. "Bernliner descubrió una mejor manera de grabar el sonido en los surcos."
